subject.title: fix(gmail): stop watcher when OAuth renewal is invalid

question: Should Gmail watchers stop immediately on terminal OAuth renewal failure rather than remain serving in a degraded state?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible operational policies, and the issue allows either a terminal/degraded state or monitorable health; selecting immediate shutdown changes an existing operator-visible failure mode.

options.title: Accept fail-closed shutdown
options.body: After live proof, stop or refuse the watcher on confirmed terminal OAuth errors so stale Gmail coverage cannot appear healthy.

options.title: Keep a degraded watcher state
options.body: Revise the design to keep the listener running while exposing explicit unhealthy status and bounded terminal-error reporting.

options.title: Accept without live proof
options.body: Merge the classifier based on mocked tests and accept uncertainty around actual Gog error strings and transient retry behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed shutdown
recommendation.body: After live proof, stop or refuse the watcher on confirmed terminal OAuth errors so stale Gmail coverage cannot appear healthy.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature-history trail most strongly connects this person to the watcher and foreground service behavior being changed.
